articles.title: Truck Flattens Power Dept Bolero on Nainital Highway, Driver Killed; CCTV Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Rampur: A Bolero driver was crushed to death after a truck loaded with wood chips overturned onto his vehicle on the Nainital Highway near the Pahadi Gate intersection under the Ganj Kotwali area on Sunday evening.

body.html:
Rampur: A Bolero driver was crushed to death after a truck loaded with wood chips overturned onto his vehicle on the Nainital Highway near the Pahadi Gate intersection under the Ganj Kotwali area on Sunday evening.

The accident occurred around 4.45 pm when both vehicles were heading towards Bilaspur Gate. Police said the Bolero, which was ahead of the truck, attempted to turn near the intersection. The truck driver tried to avoid a collision, hit the divider, broke it and overturned onto the Bolero, burying it under wood chips.

The Bolero was on contract with the Electricity Department and assigned to the Sub-Divisional Officer posted at the Khoud Electricity Sub-Station. The SDO was not in the vehicle at the time. The driver, identified as Firasat, a resident of Gujar Tola, was pulled out in critical condition and taken to the district hospital, where he was declared dead.

Traffic came to a halt for nearly an hour. Police from Ganj, Civil Lines and the city police station, along with traffic police, fire brigade teams and ambulances, reached the spot. Superintendent of Police Vidyasagar Mishra and CO City Jitendra Kumar supervised the rescue. A crane was used to remove the overturned truck and clear the highway.

The truck driver fled the scene. Police said the truck has a Rampur registration and efforts are on to trace the absconding driver. An investigation into possible overloading is underway. CCTV footage of the accident has surfaced and is being widely shared on social media.

articles.title: Drunken Rage Turns Deadly: Kanpur Woman Batters Husband to Death with Rolling Pin and Grinding Stone
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 45-year-old man was beaten to death by his wife during a drunken argument in Tikra village under the Bithoor police station area of Kanpur on Wednesday night. The deceased has been identified as Ravishankar Savita alias Pappu.

body.html:
A 45-year-old man was beaten to death by his wife during a drunken argument in Tikra village under the Bithoor police station area of Kanpur on Wednesday night.

The deceased has been identified as Ravishankar Savita alias Pappu. Police said his wife, Veerangna, first attacked him with a rolling pin until it broke and then struck him more than two dozen times with a mortar and pestle on the head, face, hands and neck.

Bithoor Inspector Premnarayan Vishwakarma said both the husband and wife were intoxicated and had a history of frequent disputes after drinking. Veerangna had returned home around 8 pm from her sister’s place in a drunken state, while Ravishankar came back late from work. An argument later escalated into a violent fight.

During the scuffle, Veerangna also suffered a head injury. Around 3 am, she informed family members that her husband had been injured in an “accident”. When relatives reached the house, she was allegedly cleaning blood from the courtyard. Police were alerted and a forensic team collected evidence from the spot, including bloodstained clothes found on the stairs.

Ravishankar, who worked as a tile and stone installer, was taken to hospital, where he died during treatment. Post-mortem findings revealed around 26 injury wounds, with death caused by excessive bleeding leading to coma.

Police said the accused initially resisted when they arrived but later confessed during interrogation. A murder case has been registered on the complaint of the victim’s brother Santosh.

The couple had married in 2019 and have a four-year-old son, Jain. They had been living separately from Ravishankar’s parents for about five years, around a kilometre away. The child, terrified after seeing his father bleeding, hid in a room. He was later handed over to Santosh.

Before being sent to jail on court orders, Veerangna kissed her son and told police she had made a grave mistake, asking her brother-in-law to take care of the child.

Police said both spouses were addicted to alcohol and often quarrelled, with several complaints earlier reported at the local outpost. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Real-Life Drishyam in UP: Man Strangles Wife, Buries Body Behind Home in Gorakhpur
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A missing woman case in Uttar Pradesh’s Gorakhpur has turned into a chilling murder, with a man accused of strangling his wife and burying her body in a pit behind their house.

body.html:
A missing woman case in Uttar Pradesh’s Gorakhpur has turned into a chilling murder, with a man accused of strangling his wife and burying her body in a pit behind their house.

The accused, Arjun, a labourer who works in Ludhiana, allegedly killed his 26-year-old wife Khushbu on December 21 after suspecting her of secretly using a mobile phone and being in touch with another man. The couple had been married for two years and had no children.

After the incident, Arjun told family members that Khushbu had left home without informing anyone. When she could not be traced for days, his father Shyam Narayan approached the police, suspecting that his son had killed his daughter-in-law.

During interrogation, Arjun first claimed Khushbu died by suicide and that he dumped her body in a river. He even took police to the riverbank and misled them for nearly two hours. As contradictions emerged, he allegedly confessed.

Police said Arjun admitted to strangling Khushbu around 11 pm and burying her in a six-foot-deep pit behind the house. On Thursday, police excavated the spot and recovered the body, which was sent for post-mortem.

Circle Officer Shilpa Kumari said the body was recovered based on the accused’s confession. A murder case has been registered on a complaint by Khushbu’s younger brother, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Drunk Navy Officer Thrashes Traffic Cop in Vizag, Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A Navy officer was arrested after allegedly assaulting a traffic policeman while under the influence of alcohol in the Malkapuram area of Visakhapatnam.

body.html:
A Navy officer was arrested after allegedly assaulting a traffic policeman while under the influence of alcohol in the Malkapuram area of Visakhapatnam.

The incident occurred in the early hours when traffic police had stopped vehicles due to Indian Oil Corporation pipeline work on the Vizag–Malkapuram road. Traffic constable Srinivas Rao was on duty when the officer, identified as Rahul Krishna, attempted to pass through.

Police said Rahul Krishna abused and beat up Srinivas Rao when he was stopped, causing injuries. Other personnel rushed to the spot and detained him.

The accused was later arrested and sent to judicial remand. A case has been registered, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Birthday Turns into Nightmare: Bajrang Dal Storms Café in Bareilly, Police Action Sparks Outrage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A birthday celebration at a café in Prem Nagar, Bareilly, was disrupted on December 27 after members of the Bajrang Dal allegedly stormed the venue, accusing the group of “love jihad” as two Muslim youths were present with Hindu women.

body.html:
A birthday celebration at a café in Prem Nagar, Bareilly, was disrupted on December 27 after members of the Bajrang Dal allegedly stormed the venue, accusing the group of “love jihad” as two Muslim youths were present with Hindu women.

The party was hosted by a nursing student along with nine friends. Reports say over a dozen activists barged in and assaulted at least one of the Muslim boys, Shan and Waqif, and the girl host when she tried to intervene.

Police who reached the spot challaned the two youths and a café staffer for breach of peace, even as they said the students had done nothing wrong. The attackers were reportedly only advised to disperse, triggering public criticism.

After the incident went viral on social media, Bareilly SP (City) Manush Pareek said on December 28 that an FIR would be registered against the unidentified attackers. An explanation has also been sought from the local SHO for not taking immediate action against the aggressors.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Thumbnail War! Janhvi Kapoor vs Dhruv Rathee Sparks Social Media Storm #breakingnews
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Actor Janhvi Kapoor and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee landed in a controversy in late December 2025 over the timing and thumbnail of Rathee’s video on cosmetic surgeries in Bollywood.

body.html:
Actor Janhvi Kapoor and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee landed in a controversy in late December 2025 over the timing and thumbnail of Rathee’s video on cosmetic surgeries in Bollywood.

On December 25, Kapoor shared an Instagram story condemning the lynching of Hindu youth Dipu Chandra Das in Bangladesh, calling it “barbaric” and urging people to speak up. About five hours later, Rathee released a 25-minute YouTube video on “fake beauty” in Bollywood, featuring Janhvi’s alleged before-and-after images prominently in the thumbnail.

The proximity of the two posts triggered backlash, with several social media users accusing Rathee of targeting Kapoor in retaliation for her post. The issue gained traction after influencer Orry defended Kapoor, calling Rathee “anti-nationalist”.

As reels and posts went viral, netizens debated whether the thumbnail was a deliberate attempt to mock Kapoor, fuelling speculation across platforms.

Rathee later responded with a follow-up video, denying any link between his content and Kapoor’s Bangladesh post. He said there was no intent to target her and urged viewers not to believe misinformation without reasoning.

The controversy continues to trend across social media.

articles.title: In Bihar: PCS Officer Loses Three Children to Poisonous Smoke
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Chhapra, Bihar: A tragic incident unfolded in Chhapra where four members of a family, including three children, died of suffocation caused by smoke from a burning stove during the night of December 26.

body.html:
Chhapra, Bihar: A tragic incident unfolded in Chhapra where four members of a family, including three children, died of suffocation caused by smoke from a burning stove during the night of December 26.

The deceased have been identified as 3-year-old Tejas, 4-year-old Adhyay, 7-month-old Gudiya and their 70-year-old grandmother Kamlavati Devi. Tejas and Adhyay were sons of Amisha Devi and PCS officer Vijay Singh, the District Cooperative Officer of Varanasi. Gudiya was the daughter of Anjali Devi.

Four others — Amisha Devi, Anjali Devi, Amit Kumar and Amrita Devi — are in critical condition and undergoing treatment on ventilators at Ruban Hospital in Patna.

According to family members, after dinner, the family slept in a closed hall to escape the cold. Rice straw and cow dung cakes were burnt in a fireplace, which filled the air-blocked room with carbon monoxide, leading to suffocation during sleep.

By morning, there was no response from those inside. When the door was opened, smoke poured out and one family member fainted. Neighbours rushed the victims to Chhapra Sadar Hospital, from where the critically ill were referred to Patna.

On receiving the news, Vijay Singh rushed from Varanasi and broke down at the hospital. Weeping, he said he had left his sons at their grandmother’s house just three days ago and had promised to bring them chips on his return.

Gudiya’s father Deepak, who works at an ornament shop in Chhapra, also mourned the loss of his infant daughter.

Kamlavati Devi’s body was sent for postmortem at Chhapra Sadar Hospital, while the three children were cremated on Saturday evening.

Doctors said carbon monoxide, a colourless and odourless gas, spreads unnoticed and induces deep sleep before proving fatal.

The children had come to their maternal grandparents’ home to spend the winter holidays.

articles.title: Christmas Chaos in Rajasthan School: Youths Storm St. Xavier’s, Students Terrorised
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tense situation unfolded at St. Xavier’s School in Rajasthan’s Nagaur district on Christmas Day when a group of 10–15 youths allegedly vandalised the campus during a Christmas function, triggering panic among nearly 400 students present at the time, as reported by Bhaskar English.

body.html:
A tense situation unfolded at St. Xavier’s School in Rajasthan’s Nagaur district on Christmas Day when a group of 10–15 youths allegedly vandalised the campus during a Christmas function, triggering panic among nearly 400 students present at the time, as reported by Bhaskar English.

According to school director Shaitanram Changal, the youths entered the premises while students were being prepared for the programme, raised slogans, pushed students and staff, and allegedly intimidated female employees. Several students were reportedly frightened and fell amid the chaos.

School authorities said furniture was damaged, tables and chairs were overturned, and Christmas decorations were destroyed. Changal also alleged that he was physically assaulted and injured. The youths reportedly identified themselves as Bajrang Dal members and claimed they would not allow such activities.

As the situation escalated, staff confined three youths in a room and alerted the police. Kotwali Police later detained Ramnivas, Kishan Khosa and a juvenile, said to be Ramnivas’s son.

The incident has drawn sharp reactions from the Private School Association, which demanded strict action. State Secretary Vinay Sharma confirmed that an FIR has been registered and warned of statewide protests if justice is denied. He also said the association would approach the High Court if required.

Kotwali Police Station officer Vedpal Shivran said the matter is under investigation and action will follow. The incident has once again raised concerns over student safety during school celebrations.

articles.title: Love, Betrayal and Murder: Wife, Cousin Arrested for Killing Man in UP
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking crime, a 32-year-old man was shot dead allegedly by his wife and cousin following an illicit relationship in Kachhwa town of Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh. The victim, Saddam Ali, a resident of Jaunpur, was living with his wife Savita at Kanshiram Awas.

body.html:
In a shocking crime, a 32-year-old man was shot dead allegedly by his wife and cousin following an illicit relationship in Kachhwa town of Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh.

The victim, Saddam Ali, a resident of Jaunpur, was living with his wife Savita at Kanshiram Awas. Police said Savita was having an affair with Saddam’s cousin Arbaaz Ali. The two allegedly conspired to eliminate Saddam, who had objected to their relationship.

On Thursday night, when Saddam returned home from the market, he reportedly found the two together, leading to an argument. During the altercation, Arbaaz allegedly shot him with a country-made pistol. The accused then tried to pass off the death as electrocution and raised an alarm.

Saddam was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead and found bullet injuries, prompting a police probe.

Based on a complaint by Saddam’s father Salim Ansari, police registered a murder case. Both Savita and Arbaaz were arrested and sent to jail. A .32 bore pistol and two cartridges were recovered.

Senior officers, including ASP Nagar Nitesh Kumar Singh, said further investigation is underway.
